chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ali ibn Ribat and Al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn Al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the orphan girl, when should her wealth be handed over to her? He said: When you know that she will neither spoil it nor waste it.
So I asked him, if she had married? He said: If she were to get married, the possession (authority) of the executor is cut-off from her.
ai.seo_question: When should an orphan girl's wealth be handed over to her according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the release of an orphan's wealth hinges on practical financial prudence ('not spoiling or wasting') rather than mere biological maturity, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of 'bulugh' (adulthood) being tied to 'rushd' (sound judgment). Furthermore, the immediate cessation of the guardian's authority upon marriage highlights the legal transition of financial independence, a nuance distinct from some other schools of thought that may link guardianship solely to age or specific milestones.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ali Bin Rabaat and Al Husayn Bin Hashim and Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the orphan girl, when should her wealth be handed over to her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it is known that she would neither spoil it nor waste it’.
So I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘If she got married?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If she were to get married, the possession (authority) of the executor is cut-off from her’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from Ali ibn Ribat and al-Husayn ibn Hashim and from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Is ibn al-Qasim who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about the case of a female orphan; when her assets must be given to her. He (the Imam) said, ‘When you learn that she does not destroy it or lose it, then you can give it to her.’
I then asked, ‘What happens if she has married?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘When she marries then possession (authority) of executor of the will ends.’”
